<module id="LIFObuffer">
    <description>A 4-bit wide Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) buffer for temporary data storage.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="dataIn" width_description="[3:0]">4-bit input data to be pushed onto the buffer.</input>
        <input id="RW">Read/Write control signal (1 for read, 0 for write).</input>
        <input id="EN">Enable signal to activate buffer operations.</input>
        <input id="Rst">Active high reset signal to initialize the buffer.</input>
        <input id="Clk">Clock signal for synchronous operations.</input>
        <output id="EMPTY">Flag indicating whether the buffer is empty.</output>
        <output id="FULL">Flag indicating whether the buffer is full.</output>
        <output id="dataOut" width_description="[3:0]">4-bit output data retrieved from the buffer.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="SP">Stack Pointer, tracks the current position in the stack.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <signal id="dataIn_reg" type="reg" width_description="[3:0]">Register to store the input data during clock cycle.</signal>
        <signal id="RW_reg" type="reg">Register to store the Read/Write signal during clock cycle.</signal>
        <signal id="EN_reg" type="reg">Register to store the enable signal during clock cycle.</signal>
        <signal id="Rst_reg" type="reg">Register to store the reset signal during clock cycle.</signal>
        <signal id="Clk_reg" type="reg">Register to store the clock signal during clock cycle.</signal>
        <signal id="EMPTY_reg" type="reg">Register to store the EMPTY flag during clock cycle.</signal>
        <signal id="FULL_reg" type="reg">Register to store the FULL flag during clock cycle.</signal>
        <signal id="dataOut_reg" type="reg" width_description="[3:0]">Register to store the output data during clock cycle.</signal>
        <signal id="SP_reg" type="reg" width_description="[2:0]">Register to store the Stack Pointer value during clock cycle.</signal>
        <signal id="stack_mem" type="reg" width_description="[3:0]" length="4">Array of registers representing the stack memory to store data.</signal>
        <always @(posedge Clk_reg or posedge Rst_reg)> // Sequential logic block triggered on positive edge of Clk_reg or Rst_reg
            if (Rst_reg == 1'b1) begin // Check if Rst_reg is active-high
                SP_reg <= 3'd4; // Set SP_reg to initial value of 4
                EMPTY_reg <= 1'b1; // Set EMPTY_reg to indicate the stack is initially empty
                FULL_reg <= 1'b0; // Set FULL_reg to indicate the stack is initially not full
                dataOut_reg <= 4'h0; // Initialize dataOut_reg to zero
                dataIn_reg <= 4'h0; // Initialize dataIn_reg to zero
                RW_reg <= 1'b0; // Initialize RW_reg to zero
                EN_reg <= 1'b0; // Initialize EN_reg to zero
                stack_mem[0] <= 4'h0; // Initialize first element of stack_mem to zero
                stack_mem[1] <= 4'h0; // Initialize second element of stack_mem to zero
                stack_mem[2] <= 4'h0; // Initialize third element of stack_mem to zero
                stack_mem[3] <= 4'h0; // Initialize fourth element of stack_mem to zero
            end else if (EN_reg == 1'b1) begin // Check if EN_reg is enabled
                dataIn_reg <= dataIn; // Store input data in dataIn_reg
                RW_reg <= RW; // Store Read/Write signal in RW_reg
                EN_reg <= EN; // Store enable signal in EN_reg
                Rst_reg <= Rst; // Store reset signal in Rst_reg
                Clk_reg <= Clk; // Store clock signal in Clk_reg
                if (RW_reg == 1'b0 && FULL_reg == 1'b0) begin // Write operation and stack is not full
                    SP_reg <= SP_reg - 3'd1; // Decrement stack pointer
                    stack_mem[SP_reg] <= dataIn_reg; // Push data into stack memory
                    EMPTY_reg <= 1'b0; // Set EMPTY_reg to false since stack is not empty
                    if (SP_reg == 3'd0) begin // Check if stack pointer reaches zero
                        FULL_reg <= 1'b1; // Set FULL_reg to true since stack is full
                    end
                end else if (RW_reg == 1'b1 && EMPTY_reg == 1'b0) begin // Read operation and stack is not empty
                    dataOut_reg <= stack_mem[SP_reg]; // Pop data from stack memory
                    stack_mem[SP_reg] <= 4'h0; // Clear the memory location after popping
                    SP_reg <= SP_reg + 3'd1; // Increment stack pointer
                    FULL_reg <= 1'b0; // Set FULL_reg to false since stack is not full
                    if (SP_reg == 3'd3) begin // Check if stack pointer reaches maximum index
                        EMPTY_reg <= 1'b1; // Set EMPTY_reg to true since stack is empty
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>Implemented using sequential logic to manage stack pointer and flags based on input signals.</implementation>
</module>
